guidelinesCompliance.guideline: New public APIs must be documented.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: All public renderer value types, constructors, accessors, errors, limits, and output methods have rustdoc in src/features/weekly_radar/interface/telegram_renderer.rs.

guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Do not import internal modules from other features.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: Renderer source imports only std::collections and std::fmt; source-boundary tests reject crate, org_x, network, and runtime provider imports.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: All requested sections are rendered in deterministic priority order.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Important Structural Change, Stage Transition, Top5, Threshold Distance, Rising, Dropped, System Health, and explicit No Change facts appear in documented order.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Focused and same-stem companion tests assert every supplied fragment and every section marker order.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Full Markdown fragments and company cards remain atomic.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Complete supplied Markdown remains in output; item, card, character, and line overflow returns an error without partial or truncated output.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Focused tests cover item/card/character/line limit errors and assert complete card fragments are never shortened.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Explicit inputs are formatted without domain recomputation.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The renderer preserves supplied labels and Markdown and contains no Stage, Ranking, Distance, provider, or Publisher calculation/import.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Source assertions, fmt, Clippy, all tests, and reference-impact evidence passed.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Invalid input and explicit No Change state are deterministic.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Blank values, duplicate identities, period mismatch, missing/contradictory change state, and invalid limits return typed errors; explicit No Change renders without inventing events.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Module-local and integration validation/error tests passed.

risk.detail: Renderer behavior is locally verified. Product-specific numeric Telegram limits were not provided, so the API requires caller-supplied limits and defines no default; future Publisher/Splitter Work Items must preserve atomic message blocks.

observedIssues: Initial ai-start Preflight was not_ready because the skeleton lacked raw request, intent, concrete acceptance, sources, and scenario coverage; resolved by completing the current Contract and rerunning ai-preflight to ready.
Initial cargo fmt check reported formatting differences; resolved with cargo fmt --all and the subsequent format check passed.

residualRisks.detail: Publisher, HTTP, sensitive runtime configuration, retries, splitting, and persistence remain outside this WI; later adapters must consume the complete TelegramMessage without re-deriving facts or truncating cards.
No product-specific line or character values were provided; callers must select TelegramRenderLimits explicitly until a later Contract supplies a product policy.

reviewReadiness.reason: All required verification passed; residual risk remains documented.

followUps: WI-WR-010 may implement a Telegram Publisher Adapter that consumes TelegramMessage without recalculating facts.
WI-WR-011 may implement semantic message splitting while preserving complete Markdown blocks and company cards.
knownGaps: Product-specific numeric Telegram limits were not provided; the renderer intentionally requires caller-supplied limits instead of inventing defaults.

intentAlignment.rationaleValidated: The tests and reference-impact scan show deterministic explicit-fact formatting with atomic limit errors while Publisher/provider and domain-calculation concerns remain outside the boundary.

overclaimPrevention: Claims are limited to fresh local test, formatter, Clippy, source-boundary, and later AI Cockpit Finish evidence; hosted provider publication and remote lifecycle actions are not claimed.
